claims.claim: The registry has a reviewing guide for auditors and a dropped-attestations list.
claims.method: Both files exist on HEAD. The guide describes ERC-8176 hashing, EAS offchain attestations and PR submission to a sigs folder.

claims.claim: All attestations in the registry are signed by one firm.
claims.method: On 2026-11-28 the repository tree has 169 sig files under registry/*/sigs, and all 169 file names carry the same signer address 0x3846c3A30E62075Fa916216b35EF04B8F53931f6. The dropped-attestations list names Cyfrin as auditor in each row. The proposal counted 166 on 2026-10-31.
The repository tree on 2026-11-28 holds 1,937 calldata and EIP-712 descriptor files, a different unit than the proposal's count. The 2026-10-31 snapshot was not rebuilt.

claims.claim: Sourcify's dashboard shows the top 100 contracts carry 75% of non-transfer calls, 20 with a descriptor and 0 attested.
claims.method: The dashboard is a JavaScript app and returned only its page shell.

claims.claim: Bybit lost about $1.5 billion in February 2025 after signers approved a Safe transaction whose displayed contents differed from what they signed.
claims.method: NCC Group text describes malicious JavaScript injected into the Safe{Wallet} UI through a compromised developer machine, causing signers to authorize a different transaction. The Bybit timeline page returned no content to automated requests.
